title: Uttanka and the hunter's water
hookLine: a sage in the desert hears the war is over and threatens to curse Krishna for not stopping it
carry: sama-darshana: the wise see God in every giver
tomorrow: a child is born without breath. can Krishna's promise hold?

lines: HE RAISES HIS HAND TO CURSE.
cards: Krishna is heading home to Dwaraka across a desert when he meets an old friend: the sage Uttanka, who has spent a long time in austerity and hasn't heard the news. Uttanka greets him warmly.
So, did you make peace between the cousins? Krishna tells him the truth. There was no peace.
The Kauravas are dead. And the sage's face changes. You could have stopped it, Uttanka says, and you didn't.
He raises his hand to curse the man standing in front of him.

teach.b: Krishna doesn't flinch, and he doesn't argue first. Hear me out, he says, and then decide. He tells Uttanka he went to the Kauravas himself and they would not listen.
Then, in the epic's telling, he shows Uttanka the same vast universal form Arjuna saw before the battle: the whole world inside God. The sage lowers his hand.

Krishna offers him a gift, and Uttanka asks for something simple: water, whenever he needs it in this dry country. Think of me, Krishna says. Some time later Uttanka is wandering, desperately thirsty, and he remembers.

teach.h: AN OUTCAST HUNTER OFFERS A DRINK
teach.b: Toward him comes a hunter, an outcast by the rules of the time, filthy, surrounded by dogs, offering water. Uttanka is disgusted and sends him away. Then Krishna appears.

That was Indra, king of the gods, bringing you amrita, the drink of immortality, in that form, to see what you would do. Uttanka turned down immortality because of who was holding the cup. Here's the teaching.
In the Gita, Krishna says the wise see the same in a learned priest, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcast.

teach.h: SAMA-DARSHANA: THE SAME GOD IN EVERY GIVER
teach.b: Hindus call it sama-darshana, equal vision: one divine Self living in every being. Uttanka had just seen God holding the whole world, and minutes later couldn't see God in one dusty man with dogs.
Many teachers read the story as exactly that gap. Today the test rarely looks holy. It looks like the person you'd rather not take anything from.

how: Uttanka's meeting with Krishna is told in the Ashvamedhika Parva, and storytellers retell Indra's disguised gift alongside the Gita's teaching of equal vision: the same God in every giver.

o: a rite to bring rain in a desert country
the drink of immortality the gods all share
the book of the horse sacrifice and its journeys

games.q: the sage in the desert — tap the pairs.

s: he raises his hand to, but listens first and lowers it.
Krishna explains that Indra brought amrita in that form.
the Gita says the wise see a priest and an outcast differently
Gita 5.18: the wise see the same in a priest, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast.

games.q: you're Uttanka. you've just seen Krishna's universal form, the whole world inside God. now a filthy hunter with dogs offers you water. by the Gita's equal vision, what fits?
o: drink, and thank him: the same God lives in him.
refuse; a holy man shouldn't take water from someone like that.
wait for a more respectable person to come by.
games.why: Uttanka refused, and it was Indra carrying amrita. sama-darshana, equal vision, sees one divine Self in every being.

practice: Put your palms together at your chest, the way Hindus greet each other with namaste, which many explain as the divine in me bowing to the divine in you.

Bring to mind someone whose help you'd refuse because of who they are, how they look, or what they once did. Picture them holding out something you need, notice honestly what rises in you, and bow to them silently, just a little.
If you pray, hold them in your prayer, just as they are; if you don't, simply let the bow stand.

wordCard.voice: Ashvamedhika. The book where a sage refuses the drink of immortality because of who was holding the cup.

orig.note: amrita: the drink of immortality that Indra brought in disguise.

carryVoice: Your line: sama-darshana, the wise see God in every giver. The hunter with the dogs was carrying amrita. Day eight hundred sixty-nine, done.
